I play and have played a smattering of mmos, most I joined for interest in the subject matter, this one just looked good. And it pays out in spades. The trailer shows te incredible synergy between classes, weapons and abilities, almost too perfect. But it does what it says on the box, very little of the trailer is beyond the abilities of players in game. 

Players essentially inhabit gun-toting space ninjas, and if those words in a chain don't cinch the deal, I don't know what will. Knee-sliding pistol-firing attacks, flying kicks with a bladed quarterstaff, lase sniper rifles, throwing stars and several flavors of superpower round out a collection of bad guy disposal options to rival any game on the market.

The arrangement of weapons is good and getting better, a diverse array of options allow any playstyle I've yet seen to perform. The abilities available to the player characters are for the most part highly effective, without being overpowered or unbalanced. Further, customization of character, weapons, companion and visual style are driven by a system veritably loaded with options. 

The grind is a bit tedious at times, and the community of individuals is often....terse, but these are the pitfalls of an mmo, and I can hardly fault this game for failing to break the mold. 

Monetization is mildly inconvenient but handled with grace. Most of the excellent options in game can be had with some level of grinding, or they can be purchased outright. Therese an upgrade mechanic that offers a $1-2 option to increase effectiveness, or grind the same bonus out over the course of a few days. I don't see the price as unfair, and the grind isn't overlong if one knows where to go. The game recieves frequent patches, hotfixes and updates, every few weeks it seems the game gets something new.

Overall, the game is fun and handles it's mmo aspects as well as can be expected. Give it a try.

AN AMAZING FREE TO PLAY GAME... played it since closed beta now that its open beta, don't regret trying it out during closed beta. SEEN ALL THE CHANGES THAT THIS PUBLISER/DEVELOPER did to this game. Game doesn't force u to pay to get items faster but its a FREE TO PLAY Game the developers need the money to put food on their tables. But you don't have to pay any real world money to get any items such as weapons, and warframes (different charaters you can play as) but it may take a while, and a lot of grinding. However my rig is very old but varies between 10fps to 30 fps on it but on most rigs it has a steady 60+ fps on more up-to-date hardware.   OVERALL VERY GREAT FREE TO PLAY GAME.

With too many hours blown on the game (Was an Original founder/Excalibur Prime era owner/player.), this is my thoughts:

- The grind isn't all that bad, suck it up.. any other MMO would have you grinding. 
- Parkour 2.0 sucks, slowed us all down more than likely due to some whiner who couldn't 'copter/wall   jump/climb. 
- The past few non-Prime Frames have been meh.. With that being said, all the Primes need a boost over their normal frame types.. the differences other than cosmetic are too minimal. 
- Vauban is NOT easy mode, and thankfully not trendy. 
- DE needs to be more thorough with their testing before updates come out. 
- Weapon choices for end-game (see: Void/Derelict/8 man mission) are minimal. 
- Archwing sucks, and needs a total rework IMO. 
- Kubrow/Katbrow are great conceptual ideas, but poorly implemented. The sentinels do a way better job. 
- Game hosting for area sessions I think need dedicated servers to run, not peer to peer bs. 

After coming back from a year off, it seems like DE took Warframe and set it to rot.. not caring about their own originality or updates, as much as they seem like they give a damn through their Devstreams. 

7/10? maaaaybe... still addictive to a point.

Get ready to dive into the diverse world of Warframe.
I had a lot of fun with it, back when I played it with my friends. Playing along my friends was more like a "So what mission do you want to try now? What type of Warframe are you trying to create now? Oh, let's get this weapon!", but now it became more serious, packed with new maps, new quests, tons of terms that can be overwhelming... now it feels something like "Man, I have to do this mission for the 5th time for the loot... I also think I'm going to do it with Saryn since it's most effective here... yeah, I like this weapon, but it's damage it's not that high..."
It felt like I had to put some fun aside to get better at the game. 

Don't misjudge me, I enjoy playing it, every part of it, but if you venture intro Warframe, prepare for some repetitive parts.
